title: Do Female Directors Raise ESG Ratings? A Meta-Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2609.28549v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Appointing more women to corporate boards is widely expected to also raise firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. We provide the first meta-analysis of this relationship, drawing on 533 estimates from 106 studies that measure ESG performance with Bloomberg or LSEG ratings. The average reported effect of a one-percentage-point increase in board gender diversity is about 0.28 ESG points, but much of it does not survive scrutiny. Correcting for publication bias with a battery of linear and non-linear methods lowers the effect to between roughly 0.08 and 0.17 points. A best-practice estimate that also imposes sound study design puts it near 0.12 for most of the world, markedly higher for the Middle East, and near -0.11 for the Southeast Asian markets that dominate the Asian evidence. translated_title: 女性董事能否提高ESG评级？一项元分析研究
translated_abstract: 任命更多女性进入公司董事会被普遍认为也能提升企业的环境、社会与治理（ESG）表现。本文对这一关系进行了首次元分析，基于106项使用彭博或LSEG评级衡量ESG表现的研究，共纳入533个估计值。董事会性别多样性每增加一个百分点，文献报告的平均效应约为0.28个ESG点，但其中很大一部分经不起严格检验。通过一系列线性和非线性方法对发表偏倚进行校正后，效应降至约0.08至0.17个点之间。进一步采用良好研究设计的最佳实践估计显示，在世界上大部分地区该效应约为0.12，在中东地区明显更高，而在主导亚洲证据的东南亚市场则约为-0.11。研究间剩余的差异具有系统性，主要由地理因素和估计方法的选择所驱动。
tldr: 首个针对女性董事与ESG评级关系的元分析表明，在纠正发表偏倚后，女性董事对ESG评级的正向效应大幅缩小（约0.08至0.17个点），且效应因地区而异——在中东较高，而在东南亚市场甚至为负。
en_tdlr: The first meta-analysis of female directors' impact on ESG ratings shows that the reported positive effect shrinks substantially after correcting for publication bias (to roughly 0.08–0.17 points), with systematic regional differences—higher in the Middle East and even negative in Southeast Asian markets.
